title: Stonebeck: marks lag as spreads gap wider

rating: underweight

The headline gap between reported and public marks — +9.5% — is, in our house's structural reading, the single most informative number on the page.¹ It suggests that the -18.0% drawdown investors can see is not the full picture but a floor beneath which reported valuations have yet to catch up. Where some read the one_year_return of +3.3% as evidence of resilience, we read it as a lagging indicator: a number computed before the newsflow's bear-market confirmation and the spread widening now visible in credit.

On spreads: hy_spread_now_bps at 780bps, moving wider "on default fears," is precisely the kind of fragility our prior treats as compounding rather than self-correcting. The view that "policy support resolves the stress" presumes the central bank has room to ease. We are less sanguine — cpi_now at 4.1% against a policy_rate_now of 5.25% leaves a positive real rate that constrains any dovish pivot. Policy support may arrive, but not on the timeline the stress requires.

Picture a chart with two lines: the reported mark, gently declining, and the public price, falling faster and further, the gap between them widening left to right like a slowly opening pair of scissors. That is the reported_vs_public_gap made visual, and it is the chart we would want before endorsing "stay the course."

The explicit risk to our view: should the central bank ease meaningfully despite the inflation print — a scenario the newsflow does not currently support but cannot be ruled out — spreads could compress quickly and the marks-lag thesis would look excessively cautious. We flag this as a live risk to monitor, not a rebuttal.
